content:
In the past few days, two reports have pointed out the different ways Apple could increase profitability by boosting its services revenue.

In my view, Apple absolutely should pursue the first approach, but not the second — and it looks like Phil Schiller might agree with this take……

Let me first summarise the contents of these two reports.

Home security and monitoring service

On Friday, Bloomberg reported that Apple may be planning to launch a brand-new home security and monitoring service, to go with some of the new home hardware we're expecting.

Squeezing more revenue from the App Store

Bloomberg's second report on Sunday said the company is looking at ways to extract more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple should not adopt the latter approach

Conversely, I believe the second approach would be a very serious mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly over iPhone app sales is already being questioned by regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell an iPhone app, you must do so through the official App Store, leaving you no choice but to accept the company's terms with no room to negotiate.

I understand there's a common view that nobody is forcing you to buy an iPhone or develop apps for it, but that view doesn't align with how even the most laissez-faire capitalism operates in practice: even in the US, there have been antitrust laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, you face behavioural constraints to ensure you don't abuse that position.

Trying to squeeze more money out of the App Store runs exactly counter to "skating to where the puck is going," and Phil Schiller reportedly agrees — Bloomberg noted this is one of the reasons for his current step-back.

Innovative services are the right direction

Instead, launching brand-new, innovative services that customers are happy to pay for is what Apple should be doing. I can easily see the value of the company offering a home security monitoring service.

I argued back in 2024 that developing its own smart home cameras would be one of the smartest moves the company could make. I expressed the same view at the time regarding the rumoured Apple smart doorbell. Adding an optional service bundle to security products is entirely sensible, for two reasons.

First, all the privacy reasons I've mentioned before apply. HomeKit Secure Video has already done a great deal to ensure the privacy of security camera footage. If there's one company I could trust to perform AI analysis on security camera footage, it would be Apple.

Second, Apple is of course best placed to fully integrate security hardware and services within the HomeKit ecosystem. I'm sure there are plenty of other areas where Apple could offer similar advantages.

For me, the key point is that Apple needs to treat services with the same attitude it applies to hardware. Make excellent products that customers are happy, smilingly willing to pay for — rather than extracting money in ways that annoy customers, developers and regulators alike.

What do you think? Please share your views in the comments section.
